newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 10.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company -- LABOUR UNDECIDED ON WINDFALL TAX SCOPE

Labour leaders remain undecided on the issue of how much money should be raised from the windfall tax on privatised utilities and which companies would be faced with the hardest parts of the levy. According to his aides, Labour leader Tony Blair wants the overall amount raised to between three and five billion stg less than the amount sought by his shadow chancellor Gordon Brown. Blair wants the bulk of the tax to fall on water and electrical companies, while the shadow chancellor sees British Telecom and BAA as potentially important sources of revenue.
-- HOUSE BUILDING SOARS IN TWO-SPEED UK ECONOMY

Recent statistics have shown a dramatic increase in UK house building and more modest growth in manufacturing, indicating evidence of a two-speed UK economy. The slower growth of manufacturing is blamed on the rise in sterling's exchange rate. The housing industry, however, fears the increase may be shortlived and are especially concerned the next government may attempt to avoid a housing boom by scrapping mortgage tax relief.
-- ALLIANZ ACTS OVER HOLOCAUST INSURANCE CLAIMS

German insurance group Allianz has taken steps to ensure Holocaust survivors' outstanding insurance claims would be honoured. The decision increases pressure on other insurers to take the same stance and on Monday, the German insurers' trade association is to hold an emergency session to discuss how they should respond. It is possible some claimants may not have taken any previous action because of postwar upheaval, language problems and reluctance to unearth past traumas.
-- TELEFONICA BOARD MEETS TO CHOOSE US TELECOMS PARTNER

The board of privatised Spanish telecommunications operator, Telefonica de Espana SA has met in Madrid in an attempt to choose a U.S. partner, a move which holds potential for significant re-alignment in global telecommunications. Rumours have Telefonica opting for MCI Communications Corp, the second-largest U.S. long distance carrier as their partner, which would indicate its turning down of global leader AT&T. Such a partnership could result in a considerable shake-up in European telecoms.
-- EUROPEAN BANKS WIN MORE SELL-OFF BUSINESS

According to a survey carried out by the journal Privatisation International, European investment banks gained a larger section of growing international privatisation advisory business in 1996. The survey shows receipts reaching record levels at $88 billion compared to $73 billion in 1995 and $64 billion in 1994. European banks increased their share of business advising governments and marketing and selling shares to investors from 45 per cent in 1995 to 60 per cent in 1996, principally at the expense of North American investment banks.
-- U.S. GROUP TAKES 50 PER CENT OF GOVERNMENT IT WORK

A report by the Treasury has confirmed that U.S.-based computer services group, Electronic Data Systems GME.N (EDS), has won over 50 per cent of all government information technology business. The disclosure is a blow to ministers who have tried to convince Commons public account committee how many contracts EDS has won. A senior Public Accounts Committee member has asked for an inquiry onto the report.
-- GAS USERS ARE FORCED TO WAIT ON PRICE RULES

An inquiry by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission into tough price control proposals for pipeline monopoly British TransCo has been extended until May, to review new information received in the last few weeks. Gas industry regulator Ofgas rejected suggestions it had given the panel new information in order to delay a possible negative verdict. The original deadline for the report was Monday, April 14.
-- JAPANESE CARS TOP POLL OF CONSUMERS

For the fourth consecutive year, UK consumers have ranked Japanese models ahead of European-produced cars in the annual JD Power survey of consumer satisfaction. Toyota models were ranked number one and two, with Honda third and Subaru fourth. Czech auto maker Skoda was fifth, whereas BMW and Jaguar came in at only seventh and 11th respectively. UK market leader Ford has dismissed the survey as unrepresentative.
-- PROCTER & GAMBLE TO BUY TAMBRANDS FOR 1.16 BILLION STG

The U.S. consumer products group Procter & Gamble announced on Wednesday its largest acquisition with the purchase of Tambrands, the U.S. maker of Tampax, for 1.16 billion stg. Gordon Pepper chairman and chief executive of Procter & Gamble stated that the acquisition provides "a unique opportunity for Procter & Gamble to enter the tampon category with an established brand".
-- MARGINS HIT AUTOMOTIVE

Margins at Automotive Precision Holdings have been reduced due to the intense competition which led to a six per cent fall in pre-tax profits to 5.76 million stg in 1996. Chairman Brian Stairs stated that while attempting to maintain 1996 levels some new contracts carried "lower margins than the business they replace, which will have a significant effect on earnings for the foreseeable future".
